summary: I checked this independently and the auditor's DONE holds. PR #710 (60633eff3) added fetchWithDeadline, a 5 s deadline that covers both headers and body. It races the fetch, so it still works when an adapter ignores the abort signal, and it avoids AbortSignal.timeout/any so it runs on React Native. All four boot and reconnect control-plane fetches now go through it: session, bootstrap exchange, descriptor and ws-token. The deadline error is named TimeoutError and counts as transient. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken is now wrapped in retryTransientBootstrap and honours the attempt signal. protocol.ts bounds the WS URL provider with Effect.timeoutOrElse (10 s), which interrupts the provider (its signal aborts) and fails with WsUrlProviderError, so the reconnect schedule keeps advancing. The web primary, device and saved-direct transports plus mobile all set it. Once the 15 s budget runs out, the root beforeLoad rejects into RootRouteErrorView, which offers Try again (invalidates the router and re-runs beforeLoad, with the cached promises cleared) and Reload. I looked for gaps the fix might have opened. One candidate: the desktop now loads the renderer at http-bound, and the server startup gate holds API requests for up to 10 s, so a slow runtime build of more than ~16 s fails the boot reads. The desktop covers this by reloading at ready any app load requested more than 9 s earlier, so it is not a regression. Device-frame URL resolution passes no signal, but its fetches go through the same deadline-plus-retry path, so it is bounded at about 16 s.

evidence.note: fetchWithDeadline: a manual timer plus a 'stopped' race covers headers (:89-92) and body (:97-103). Caller abort settles early (:79-85). Deadline error is named TimeoutError (:20-28). No TDZ, unhandled-rejection or leak issues found; a timer that outlives an unread non-ok body just aborts the finished request at 5 s.

retryTransientBootstrap treats TypeError, AbortError/TimeoutError and 502-504 as transient, with a 15 s budget (worst case ~16 s with 5 s attempts) and a caller-signal abandon check (:123, :131, :135).

fetchControlPlane uses fetchWithDeadline for fetchSessionState (:145), requestWebSocketToken (:156), exchangeBootstrapCredential (:202). issuePrimaryWebSocketToken (:192-201) is now retried and signal-aware. The boot prefetch (:303-307) has the same deadline.

withUrlProviderTimeout uses Effect.timeoutOrElse (Effect 4.0.2 interrupts the source, which aborts the tryPromise signal) and fails with WsUrlProviderError, which the retry at :351 retries. WS_URL_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 at :143.

The primary /ws transport sets urlProviderTimeoutMs, as do the dedicated device transport (:996) and saved direct environments (:1106; desktop-SSH deliberately excluded). apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:357 does the same.

Boot awaits the descriptor and auth gate. A rejection reaches errorComponent RootRouteErrorView (:85, :435), whose Try again calls router.invalidate (:511-513). pendingReadyRootContext, bootstrapPromise and descriptorPromise are all cleared in finally, so a retry issues fresh requests.
The server gate holds API requests for up to 10 s (then 503 Retry-After). The client's 5 s deadline plus retry cycles through it, and the 503 counts as transient.

EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS = 9_000: at ready, the desktop reloads a window whose early app load is older than 9 s and has not reported a usable shell. This covers a slow runtime build exceeding the ~16 s client budget, so the deadline does not strand the desktop on the error view (wired at apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1728-1757).

Tests: a hung ws-token is retried (:158), an abandoned attempt stops retrying (:173), the session read is bounded (:190). fetchWithDeadline.test.ts:34-118 covers deadline, body, success, ignored-abort and caller-cancel. wsTransport.test.ts:335-352 checks that the URL-provider timeout aborts the first signal and starts a fresh attempt.

fixDefects: None verified. Out-of-scope observations only: (1) the generic get/post/getHubOrNull helpers (primaryAuth.ts:256-293) still call httpClient.fetch with no deadline. They serve user-initiated settings and Hub panels, not boot or reconnect. Their doc comment at :279-281 (pre-existing since 7a1f42bf5) wrongly says they inherit the transient-bootstrap retry. (2) Device-frame URL resolution (service.ts:1005) passes no signal, but it stays bounded at ~16 s by the deadline plus retry. (3) During an outage, each 10 s URL-provider window now polls ws-token every 500 ms, instead of once per backoff step. These requests are tiny and the change is harmless.
decisionReason: Nothing remains. The fix touches no auth semantics, hosted lifecycle ownership, Hub protocol or product trade-off.
